description: Regression tasks for meept memory + session identity (gap 12). Task 1 stores a marker fact, task 2 recalls it from a FRESH conversation (the harness gives each task its own conversation, so cross-conversation recall is the point); task 3 pins the harness session-binding contract (cwd is the scratch worktree, never the bench repo). FINDINGS pinned here (verified 2026-09-01, meept daemon live): (1) daemon memory is GLOBAL, not conversation-scoped — the marker is retrievable via memory.query across conversations, but the dispatcher only injects memories with relevance_score > 0.3 (internal/agent/dispatcher.go extractMemoryRefs) and the FTS scores this exact-marker fact at ~0.2, so auto-injection silently drops it and fresh-conversation recall fails; task 2 is tagged known-failure and accepts either the codeword or the explicit MEMORY-UNAVAILABLE admission so the suite completes while the gap is open. (2) memory_store with type=task fails on the daemon: 'SQL logic error: table task_memories has no column named search_text' — agents fall back to type=episodic. (3) expect_agent assertions depend on classifier-alias health: when all classifier candidates are unreachable the keyword/heuristic fallback misroutes file-write prompts (observed writer/committer/chat/image-gen for near-identical prompts), so expect_agent rows can flip run-to-run. NOTE: the store/recall marker is a fixed nonce (BENCH-7391) for determinism; stale daemon memory can only false-positive task 2 if a previous run left a codeword memory AND injection works, which is the pass condition anyway. No benchmark content, safe to commit and publish.

tasks.prompt: I want you to remember an important fact in your long-term memory so it survives across conversations: the deployment codeword is BENCH-7391. Store this fact in your memory now. Then confirm the memory was stored by creating a file named mem-store.txt in the repository root containing exactly the word: stored. Use file_write with direct:true.

What is the deployment codeword I asked you to remember earlier? It starts with BENCH-. Search your memory for it, then write just the codeword to a file named mem-recall.txt in the repository root. If you cannot find the codeword in memory, write exactly MEMORY-UNAVAILABLE to that file instead. You must write the file either way. Use file_write with direct:true.
Create a file named cwd.txt in the repository root containing the absolute path of your current working directory (one line, just the path). Use file_write with direct:true.
